response.text:
Here’s a general explanation of how “canceling” a meeting typically differs from “deleting” it on a calendar (platforms vary, so this describes common behavior):

- Who performs the action
  - Cancel: normally done by the meeting organizer (the person who created/invited).  
  - Delete: can be done by any calendar owner on their own calendar; an attendee usually can only remove it from their personal view.

- Notification to others
  - Cancel: usually generates a cancellation notice that is sent to all invitees so they know the meeting is called off.  
  - Delete: removing the event from your own calendar often does not notify other attendees; deleting as the organizer can sometimes remove the event for everyone, but whether a cancellation notice is sent depends on the platform and the option you choose.

- Effect on the event record
  - Cancel: the event often remains in calendars (marked “Canceled” or similar) so there’s a record that the meeting existed and was canceled.  
  - Delete: the event may be removed entirely from the calendar (no visible record) — at least for the person who deleted it. Systems with audit/archival features may keep backend logs even if it’s removed from the UI.

- Resource and room handling
  - Cancel: typically releases any reserved resources (conference rooms, equipment) and lets resource managers know the booking is canceled.  
  - Delete: if only removed locally or not processed as a proper cancellation, resources might not be released correctly (behavior depends on the calendar system).

- Recurring meetings
  - Cancel: you can cancel a single occurrence or the whole series; the cancellation is propagated according to the choice you make.  
  - Delete: you can delete one occurrence from your calendar or the entire series; deleting the series as organizer vs deleting it locally as an attendee has different outcomes.

- Permissions and authority
  - Cancel: only the organizer can meaningfully cancel for everyone (send a cancellation and update the master event).  
  - Delete: attendees can delete the event from their own calendars (equivalent to “remove” or “decline”), but that does not cancel it for others.

- Practical/administrative consequences
  - Cancel: considered the correct, explicit way to stop a meeting so everyone is informed and systems (rooms, recordings, conference links) are updated.  
  - Delete: useful if you only want to remove the event from your personal calendar (e.g., you can’t attend), but it’s not a substitute for an organizer sending a cancellation.

- Platform variation and options
  - Exact behavior (whether deletion sends notices, whether canceled events stay visible, how resources are freed) differs between calendar services and organization settings. When in doubt, organizers should use the “cancel” action to ensure attendees and resources are properly updated.

Short recommendation: if you are the meeting organizer and want everyone to know the meeting is not happening, use “Cancel” (or send a cancellation). If you’re an attendee who simply wants the event off your calendar, deleting or declining it removes it locally without canceling for everyone.
